2609.23892.title: Circuit-Diff: Factual Edit-based Intervention Method for Localizing Knowledge in Attribution Graphs
2609.23892.paper_summary: Mechanistic interpretability defines features as the fundamental units of a neural network and circuits as the weighted subgraphs that carry out its computation. Because individual neurons are polysemantic, Cross-Layer Transcoders (CLTs) were introduced as a way to approximate a model's circuits by generating an attribution graph. The nodes of that graph, however, are unlabeled features: reading a graph means pruning it and then working out by hand what each surviving node means. To make CLTs easier to use for circuit discovery, we introduce Circuit-Diff, which intervenes on the model itself with a low-rank factual edit and takes the features whose role in the attribution graph changes under that edit as related to the edited knowledge. On the edits we examine, the flagged nodes are not only detectors of the object token: read off the CLT's released feature dashboards, they include features for the history, geography and associations surrounding the old and new objects. We formalize the method, measure how reliable a frozen CLT remains after a factual edit, test the selected nodes causally by patching them on up to 24 CounterFact edits, give a case study, and release an open-source implementation built on the circuit-tracer package, together with two further tools (multi-prompt aggregation and rule-based supernode labeling).
2609.23892.paper_summary_zh: 機械解釋性將特徵定義為神經網絡的基本單位，而電路則是執行其計算的加權子圖。由於單個神經元是多義的，因此引入了跨層轉碼器（Cross-Layer Transcoders, CLTs）作為通過生成歸因圖來近似模型電路的一種方式。然而，該圖的節點是未標記的特徵：閱讀一個圖意味著修剪它，然後手動計算每個存活節點的含義。為了使 CLTs 更容易用於電路發現，我們引入了 Circuit-Diff，它通過低秩事實編輯對模型本身進行干預，並將在該編輯下其在歸因圖中角色發生變化的特徵視為與編輯知識相關。在我們檢查的編輯中，標記的節點不僅是物體標記的檢測器：從 CLT 釋放的特徵儀表板中讀取，它們包括舊物體和新物體周圍的歷史、地理和聯想特徵。我們對該方法進行了形式化，測量在事實編輯後凍結的 CLT 的可靠性，通過在多達 24 次 CounterFact 編輯上修補所選節點來進行因果測試，提供了一個案例研究，並發布了基於 circuit-tracer 套件的開源實現，以及兩個進一步的工具（多提示聚合和基於規則的超節點標記）。
2609.23892.author: Edward G. Friedman et.al.
